PullRequest.Title: Simplify state indicators in MCP customization page
PullRequest.Body: Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/337336 Fixes https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/338001 ## Summary Simplifies installed MCP server rows by removing status badges and using quieter, action-oriented state treatments. The final state model is: - **Running**: the default state, with no status indicator. - **Starting**: an animated spinner. - **Authentication required**: a compact **Sign In** button without a separate auth badge or icon. - **Error**: a red error icon and compact **Show Output** button. The button uses the same output routing as the context-menu action, while the ordinary server description remains visible and error details remain in the accessible label and detail view. - **Stopped**: a compact **Start** button that starts the active-session or local server. - **Disabled**: dimmed row styling, an off switch, and a plain scope label: **Disabled (Globally)**, **Disabled (Workspace)**, or **Disabled (Session)**. - **Unsupported**: red error icon and red compatibility text. - **Partially supported**: yellow warning icon and amber/yellow compatibility text. ## Additional changes - Removes configuration file paths from MCP list rows and their accessible labels while retaining Plugin and Extension provenance links. - Makes **Migrations** in compatibility messages a keyboard-accessible link to the MCP migration page. - Renames the global disable action to **Disable (Globally)** across MCP context menus, including both right-click and ellipsis menus. - Keeps every installed MCP row at the same height as the default running row. - Adds a dedicated MCP compatibility warning theme color so light themes cannot reinterpret partial-support warnings as green. - Preserves error details in screen-reader labels even though inline error snippets are no longer rendered. ## Validation - Full `npm run compile` completed with zero source errors. - Hygiene passed for all files changed by the PR. - Focused MCP list-widget unit suite passes with 90 tests. - Component Explorer includes a consolidated all-states fixture across light, dark, and high-contrast themes, plus focused error-action coverage. ## Screenshot

Scenarios.Scenario: Open or scroll the MCP customization tree and render installed server rows
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The widget groups in-memory installed/gallery entries, updates the WorkbenchObjectTree, and synchronously renders only viewport-backed row templates. Added compatibility text/icons and state controls are on this UI critical path; the alternate card-row helper is not called by production code in this file.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Total installed and marketplace entries determine tree model size, while DOM/control creation is bounded by the virtualized viewport. Compatibility parsing/link creation applies only to visible rows with a non-supported compatibility presentation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Single-threaded synchronous DOM rendering; tree virtualization recycles a bounded template set. No async fan-out is started by row rendering.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Compatibility state is read from an in-memory observable map. Tree templates, hovers, and disposable stores are recycled; no cold/warm external cache changes the path.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the renderer lifecycle, signature guard, template disposal, and production tree setup were traced directly.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Exact installed-server counts and compatibility-row prevalence vary, but active DOM cardinality remains viewport-bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The added DOM work is bounded to visible rows and disposed on recycling; no subprocess, IPC, filesystem, database, or network boundary was added to rendering.

Scenarios.Scenario: Update MCP status, enablement, compatibility, or active-session customization while the list is visible
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Observable status changes and the customization event synchronously update visible row presentation. Action DOM is rebuilt only when the status signature changes, while compatibility message content is refreshed for visible templates.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: Work scales with the virtualized visible template count for broad customization events, not the full installed collection; formatted compatibility content is a short fixed string and only creates a link for affected rows.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Updates run synchronously on the UI thread and are serialized by the event/observable delivery path; no background task or external operation is launched.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The observable compatibility map is reused. Status signatures suppress action reconstruction when state is unchanged; compatibility message listeners are replaced through bounded DisposableStores.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: both local autorun and global customization-event paths were inspected through updateStatus and their disposal ownership.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Event frequency depends on active MCP state transitions, but normal transitions are sparse and template count is viewport-bounded.
Scenarios.Verdict: No actionable performance finding. The richer compatibility refresh adds small repeated DOM work but remains bounded and does not establish realistic jank, unbounded retention, or boundary fan-out.

Scenarios.Scenario: Start a stopped MCP server from the new inline Start button
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A click resolves the current row entry and awaits exactly one server start operation. The clicked button is disabled until completion; server startup itself is the critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Start the selected local MCP server, spawning its command or connecting its configured transport.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one operation for the clicked server; no grouping or collection fan-out.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same localServer.start operation was available through existing MCP lifecycle/context-menu actions; the PR adds an inline route without increasing automatic call count.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the inline button action and required for that server to progress from Stopped.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Request the active agent host to start the selected session MCP server via target.startMcpServer.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Exactly one request for the clicked active-session server.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Existing lifecycle actions already exposed a one-server start request; the diff changes discoverability, not backend multiplicity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited by the inline Start action.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One backend start per user click and selected server. Users can initiate different rows independently, but there is no collection loop or automatic burst.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: At most one in-flight start through a given button because it is disabled around the awaited promise; there is no new shared limiter across different servers, matching existing lifecycle actions.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No UI cache is involved. Local server start is already idempotent in the MCP service path; failed or completed starts are reflected by authoritative status updates.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the click handler, awaited call, per-button disabling, and local/active-session branches were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Startup duration varies by server command and transport, but the diff does not add extra starts or collection-wide work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. This is intentional user-triggered work with one boundary call and existing lifecycle semantics.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open MCP output from an error row using the new inline Show Output button
Scenarios.CriticalPath: A click resolves the current server and invokes one existing output handler. Local servers reveal their output; active-session servers register/reuse diagnostic output state and reveal the selected channel.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Attach/reveal active agent-host MCP diagnostics for the selected server's output channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One selected output request per click; session diagnostics registration iterates that session's in-memory MCP server states and uses deduplicated registry records.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The context-menu Show Output action already called the same handler with the same selected-server cardinality; the PR adds an inline entry point.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to reveal active-session output after the user clicks Show Output.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Reveal the selected local server or output-service channel.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical output routing existed in the row context menu before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Directly completes the requested output navigation.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One selected server per click. Active-session first use records the current session's server states in memory, but the same handler and session-wide recording already backed the context-menu Show Output action.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: User-triggered promise per click with no collection-wide async fan-out. Output-channel reveal is handled by the existing output service/registry.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The active-session log registry tracks sessions and deduplicates recorded server state signatures; subsequent shows reuse registered channels. Local output uses the existing server output channel.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: inline routing was compared with getMcpServerActions and both converge on getMcpServerOutputHandler.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: First-time diagnostics setup cost depends on session server count, but the mechanism and cardinality are unchanged from the existing action.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression. The new button does not duplicate output work or amplify boundary cardinality.

Scenarios.Scenario: Open MCP Migrations from a compatibility message
Scenarios.CriticalPath: The compatibility link fires one editor event and opens the already-enabled MCP migration category. Because a category ID is supplied, this path renders the migration page directly rather than refreshing migration discovery first.
Scenarios.ScalingInput: One event and one migration-page render per explicit click; no per-server loop or automatic navigation.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Synchronous editor state/DOM update followed by a requestAnimationFrame focus; no external operation is launched on this category-specific route.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Uses current editor migration state; no cold/warm network, filesystem, or database cache participates in opening the category.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the event wiring and category-specific startCustomizationMigration/showCustomizationMigrationPage branch were traced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Migration page DOM size depends on existing migration data, but the link neither recomputes discovery nor introduces an external boundary.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance regression. The action is single-shot, user-triggered UI navigation with no new expensive boundary.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all eight changed files and all diff pages. Traced virtualized rendering, status-update lifecycle/disposal, and the Start, Show Output, and Migrations action boundaries. No high-confidence diff-introduced performance issue or concrete regression fix was found.
